beginner.description: Root-position chords only, a single bass note in the left hand, at most three notes in the right, nothing wider than an octave, no extensions and nothing outside the two octaves above middle C.

intermediate.description: Sevenths and inversions are available, the left hand may play root and fifth together, and the solver is free to invert chords to keep the right hand still.

advanced.description: Extensions up to the 13th, tenths in the left hand, and a wider register. Motion is cheap, so the solver will move a hand to reach a richer voicing.

styles.jazzy: Extensions where the level allows them, and the fifth dropped in favour of colour tones — the shell voicing a jazz pianist reaches for.
styles.sparse: As few notes as carry the harmony. Open, quiet, easy to play.
styles.lush: Full, closely spaced chords with every available tone sounding.
styles.hymn: Four-part writing with strict voice leading and minimal motion — parallel fifths are punished hard, as in a chorale.
